summary: HOS delivers the hospital edition of Nabd: inpatient admissions and a live bed board, NEWS2/PEWS escalation, barcode MAR, operating theatres with the WHO checklist, discharge with a signed summary, the emergency department (ESI triage, live board, stroke/STEMI/sepsis clocks, medico-legal register), ambulance dispatch, radiology with DICOM MWL/PACS and structured reporting (incl. India PCPNDT), blood bank with two-person checks and haemovigilance, CSSD recall, dietary, central stores, medical records with birth/death registers, and duty rosters. All of it is Phase 5 and sits behind DEC-15 (build or partner): every module can run off, native, or in partner mode through one HL7 v2/FHIR/DICOM interface seam (HOS-002, HOS-003, HOS-031), so the month-12 decision does not waste the work. Total estimate 309 engineer-days across 55 stories vs 226 days of tracker effort for the 13 in-scope tasks (1.37x); the difference is the prototype scope that the tracker one-liners do not price (NEWS2/PEWS, barcode MAR, ER pathways, pre-arrival, DICOM gateway, PCPNDT, haemovigilance, CSSD recall, three-way match, ROI checks). If DEC-15 = partner for a module, drop its native stories and keep the seam.

stories.title: Owner sets up wards, beds and bed classes for a hospital facility
stories.story: As a hospital owner/admin I want to define wards, bays and beds with their class, sex policy, isolation and tariff so that admissions, the bed board and bed-day billing all use one bed master.
stories.context: Today departments.kind already allows 'ward' (V41) and service_points.kind allows 'bed', but nothing describes a bed's clinical attributes. Beds can be blocked for maintenance with a reason. Deleting a bed that has ever held an admission is not allowed; it is retired instead. Bulk import by CSV covers a 50-200 bed nursing home in one go. stories.title: Interface engine connects a partner HIS, RIS or PACS through HL7 v2 and FHIR R4
stories.story: As the hospital engineering team we want one inbound/outbound interface layer for ADT, orders and results (HL7 v2.5.1 and FHIR R4) so that any hospital module can run in partner mode and Nabd stays the patient-facing record.
stories.context: This is the seam that makes DEC-15 cheap either way. It unblocks ward, ER and radiology users in facilities that already run a HIS or PACS, and is the base for DICOM MWL in HOS-031. Inbound: ADT A01/A02/A03/A04/A08/A11/A13 and ORM/ORU (or FHIR Encounter/ServiceRequest/DiagnosticReport) are mapped onto Nabd admissions, orders and reports through the FHIR mapping layer (T-234). Outbound: Nabd events (admission, order, report) are rendered as HL7/FHIR messages. The engine runs as an integration adapter inside core (module 'integration' under shared/integration rules: HTTP clients only there, no open transaction) with an MLLP listener exposed only on the hospital's VPN/private link. Messages are stored encrypted with tenant keys, idempotent on message control ID, and retried with a dead-letter queue visible to platform ops. PHI never enters logs; message bodies are redacted in traces. Patient matching from partner MRN uses the existing patient registry with exact-identifier match only; anything fuzzy goes to a reconciliation queue for the MRD clerk.

Given the same message control ID is delivered twice, when processed, then only one admission change is applied and the second gets ACK AA with no side effect
Given an inbound patient whose partner MRN does not exactly match a Nabd identifier, when processed, then a reconciliation item is created and no new patient is auto-created
Given a Nabd imaging order in partner mode, when it is signed, then an ORM^O01 (or FHIR ServiceRequest) is sent to the RIS within 10 s with the accession number
Given the partner endpoint is down, when 5 retries with backoff fail, then the message moves to dead-letter, an alert fires, and the owner's integrations card shows 'not sending'
Given any message, when logged, then logs contain only message type, control ID and tenant, never patient names or identifiers

stories.title: Ward nurse transfers a patient between beds or wards with a signed handover
stories.story: As a ward nurse I want to request a transfer (bed swap, ward move, ICU escalation or step-down) that the receiving nurse accepts with an SBAR handover so that the patient, their pending doses and their bill move together safely.

stories.title: Ward nurse records observations and NEWS2/PEWS is scored and escalated automatically
stories.story: As a ward nurse I want to enter observations at the bedside and get the NEWS2 (adults) or PEWS (children) score, risk level and required response instantly so that deterioration is escalated without mental arithmetic.
stories.context: NEWS2 follows the Royal College of Physicians chart with SpO2 scale 1 by default and scale 2 selectable per patient by a doctor (hypercapnic respiratory failure). Bands are as in the prototype ipd.js: total >= 7 high (emergency response, continuous monitoring), 5-6 medium (urgent review, hourly obs), any single parameter scoring 3 low-medium (urgent ward review), 1-4 low (4-6 hourly). PEWS is used for patients under 16 (age cut-off configurable) with a facility-chosen PEWS chart. Scoring logic lives in packages/domain (shared TS) and is mirrored server-side in Java with a shared fixture table so UI preview and stored score never disagree. The score is never produced by an LLM. A high score pages the rapid response team via the in-app notification and SMS fallback through comms-gateway with no patient name in the SMS. Observation frequency due times drive an 'obs overdue' flag on the board. Existing vitals table is OPD-only (unique per queue_entry), so inpatient observations get their own time-series table.

Given a total NEWS2 >= 7, when saved, then the rapid response team is paged within 30 s and the escalation is logged with who was paged and when they acknowledged
Given a 4-year-old patient, when observations are entered, then PEWS is calculated and NEWS2 is not shown
Given the 300-case fixture table, when run against both the TS and Java scorers, then all 300 scores match exactly
Given observations are due 4-hourly and none recorded for 4 h 30 min, when the board refreshes, then the bed shows 'obs overdue'

Recommendation in this spec: native IPD/OT/discharge/ER (EP41 core, NABH 3-hospital exit), partner-first for PACS image storage (HOS-031 gateway only) and optionally blood bank; HOS-002/HOS-003 make either answer cheap.

Inpatient encounter model: this spec reuses queue_entries (class='inpatient'/'emergency', V43 placeholder) as the encounter segment so clinical_notes/prescriptions/invoices FKs keep working. If the clinical/core domain splits ENCOUNTER from queue_entries first, admissions.encounter_id and er_visits.encounter_id should point there. Needs an owner decision before HOS-005/HOS-020.

T-289 (interim and consolidated IPD discharge bill, Area 'Billing & Tax') belongs to the billing domain; HOS-008 provides charge capture and HOS-018 consumes billing.discharge_bill.cleared.v1. Confirm the event contract with the billing PSE.

T-327 (complete prototype screens for hospital modules, Area 'Design & prototype') belongs to the design/frontend-foundation domain; HOS stories link to the existing ward/er/radiology/hospops screens.

T-214 (pharmacy purchase orders, GRN, suppliers) belongs to the pharmacy domain; HOS-044/HOS-046 assume one shared stock ledger and procurement model. Agree the schema with the pharmacy PSE before either is built.
T-247 (unified doctor calendar, 'busy' across facilities) belongs to the booking/identity domain; HOS-014 needs a read API (staff busy blocks) and to publish OT bookings into it.

Other cross-domain dependencies used here: T-002 break-glass (auth), T-179 secure links and T-250 Exchange custodian (consent & identity), T-206 Cedar PEP, T-224 ICD-10 search and T-303 consent capture (clinical), T-218 lab orders (lab), T-234 FHIR layer, T-237 DSR legal hold, T-094/T-095 SSE, T-123 entitlements, T-143 uploads, T-144 print, T-282 chain OLAP dashboard.
Flyway numbering: this spec uses V601-V660 for HOS migrations. Please confirm a reserved range per domain to avoid collisions.

Clinical content sign-off: NEWS2/PEWS tables, ESI/CTAS/MTS logic, pathway targets, cross-match rules and transfusion checks need the Clinical Safety Officer (T-021) and hazard-log entries before go-live. Who signs for each market?
Triage scale licensing: CTAS and MTS may need licences; ESI v4 is free. Which scales must be offered in India, UAE, KSA and Qatar?

Statutory forms (MLC, PCPNDT Form F, CRS birth/death, MCCD, HvPI, e-RaktKosh, GCC civil registration) differ by state and authority. Need counsel-confirmed form fields and whether any registry offers an API (else export/upload).

Bundled Orthanc PACS (HOS-031): if Nabd stores images, who owns image retention (UAE 25 years), storage cost and residency? Recommendation: gateway + customer/partner PACS by default; bundled Orthanc only for small nursing homes on a priced add-on.
Hardware: DEC-38 bans kiosks in clinics; confirm barcode scanners, wristband and label printers, and the on-premises DICOM gateway box are allowed in the hospital edition and who supplies them.
Roster labour rules (rest hours, max continuous hours, nurse ratios) per market and per facility: provide defaults for India and GCC, or make every facility configure them at onboarding?
Ambulance GPS: use the crew phone PWA location, a vehicle telematics partner, or manual status only for v1?
